added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed run is scan-only and its manifest names no baseline_suite or after_suite gate arm, so no base-vs-head log exists; the run changed no code or test (diff is one docs fragment), so no added failure is possible, but the count is recorded as unmeasured rather than as a measured zero per the store's own rule.

findings.text: follow-on: confirmed in source, not only in the manifest. ingest_discovered_signals Phase-2 uses MATCH (da:DataAccess {id: sig.data_access}) so a missing DataAccess silently drops every DATA_ACCESS edge, and seed_worker calls ingest_discovered_signals at :2548 before MERGEing the DataAccess node at :2574; on a first scan of any facility the edges are lost and only a second scan creates them. The node reported this; the fix (create the DataAccess node before ingesting) is in a peer-owned file.

follow-on: on the re-run that created the DATA_ACCESS edges, the CLI summary reads '12480 scanned, 0 enriched, 0 checked' and 'seed complete: 12480 items from 1 sources' while the graph holds 6240 rows. seed_worker initialises total_discovered to existing_total (6240, from the 'resumed: 0 versions, 6,240 signals in graph' line) and then adds the 6240 newly ingested, so the scan/seed summary double-counts the pre-existing baseline on every resumable run; the number is a display artifact, not a data defect, but it is not explained in the fragment or manifest.

justifications.durability: The deliverable is a graph state plus a committed fragment, not a code change, so there is no executable guard and none was warranted (the brief makes a code change conditional on the scan exposing a scanner defect, and it exposed none). The durable record is the fragment (committed at 7bd3714) and the live graph, both of which I re-read. The one carried defect, the first-scan DATA_ACCESS drop, remains untested and unfixed because it lives in a peer-owned file; the node disclosed it rather than leaving it hidden, which is the right call at this scope but leaves no regression fence behind the finding.
justifications.evidence: The record is strong but not perfect. The headline figures reproduce independently against the live graph (total 6240, 73 categories, floors met, one DataAccess, 6240 DATA_ACCESS edges, no_range 0, legacy_keywords 0, 351 null-class rows, 5889 T/O/P rows). The claimed parallel.py defect is confirmed by reading the source: seed_worker ingests signals at parallel.py:2548 before creating the DataAccess node at :2574, and ingest_discovered_signals Phase-2 is a MATCH on DataAccess (:2321), so a first scan drops every DATA_ACCESS edge. Two qualifications: the re-run log scan-attempt-4-edges.log reports 12480 scanned and 'seed complete: 12480 items' where the graph holds 6240, an unexplained double-count in the run's own evidence; and the reviewed manifest records no baseline_suite or after_suite gate arm, so the added-failure count is unmeasured rather than zero.
justifications.fit: The node runs the repaired EDAS scanner through the existing pipeline exactly as §2 requires, adds no abstraction and no new owner, and reports the parallel.py ordering defect to the coordinator instead of reaching into an out-of-scope file. The ssh -F PATH wrapper is a disclosed fence workaround, not a product change.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The §2 deliverable is met end to end and independently reproduced: the live graph holds 6240 FacilitySignal {jt-60sa, edas} across 73 categories, every row carrying shot_range and alias, with data_class set for the 5889 rows whose EDDB letter is T/O/P and left unset for the 351 outside it; the five census floors are met exactly (MAG 18, MDAC 264, PSRC 312, FAME 100, MMSYS 47 = 741) and the run spent nothing (0 enriched, Cost $0.00). My own bounded queries returned total 6240, no_range 0, legacy_keywords 0, ncats 73, edges 6240 to jt-60sa:edas:eddb, and the five floors; the fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/edas-scan.html records the census, the category table, the spot checks and the follow-ons.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff edb4bab9d..7bd3714 in the reviewed worktree lists exactly one file, docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-discovery-completion/edas-scan.html, the node's declared second write path; no scanner, schema, facility-YAML, remote-script or test path was touched, as the brief fenced. The parallel.py defect the scan exposed was reported to the coordinator as a follow-on rather than fixed in place, correctly leaving the peer-owned file alone.
